name: King of Megiddo
overview: The King of Megiddo was a male ruler known primarily for being one of the thirty-one kings defeated by Joshua during the conquest of Canaan. Specific tribal affiliation or additional personal details are not recorded in Scripture. His identity is tied to his role as a regional king in the biblical narrative of Israel's settlement in the Promised Land.
namesAndTitles: The title 'King of Megiddo' literally means 'king of Megiddo,' indicating his rulership over the city of Megiddo. This designation is a straightforward title rather than a personal name, as noted in Joshua 12:21.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture does not record any family relationships for the King of Megiddo beyond his identification as one of the kings defeated by Joshua. There are no additional relational details provided in the biblical text.
scriptureSignificance: The King of Megiddo is significant as part of the collective opposition to Israel's divinely appointed conquest under Joshua's leadership. His defeat represents the fulfillment of God's promise to give the land to Israel and demonstrates the Lord's sovereignty over the nations. This king's mention underscores the comprehensive nature of Joshua's victories in establishing Israel in Canaan.
